mn135:4.1: Kammadāyādā (‘heirs of kammas’): kammayoni here uses yoni in the sense of ‘cause’ or ‘reason’ rather than ‘womb’; kammabandhū (‘kin of kammas’) implies a binding responsibility for one’s actions.
mn135:13.1: For food, drink, clothing, and the rest as gifts, cf. Sutta 57.
mn135:15.1: For the phrase ‘due to having performed and completed’ (samattā samādinnā), cf. also Sutta 136.
